area-skill-01.target: I can explain that area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape with no gaps or overlaps.
area-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can explain that area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape with no gaps or overlaps.
area-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Counting the squares around the edge, or accepting gaps and overlaps when tiling. Try this: Tile with real square tiles; check that there are no gaps or overlaps before counting.

area-skill-02.skill: Measuring Area by Counting Unit Squares
area-skill-02.target: I can find area by counting unit squares and name it in square centimeters, square meters, square inches, square feet, or square units.
area-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can find area by counting unit squares and name it in square centimeters, square meters, square inches, square feet, or square units.
area-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Writing the unit as centimeters instead of square centimeters. Try this: Ask “What is one square worth?” and say the unit as “square ___.”

area-skill-03.skill: Area of Rectangles: Tile and Multiply
area-skill-03.target: I can find the area of a rectangle by tiling and show that multiplying the side lengths gives the same area.
area-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can find the area of a rectangle by tiling and show that multiplying the side lengths gives the same area.
area-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Adding the side lengths (finding perimeter) when area is asked. Try this: Draw rows of unit squares: the number of rows times the squares in each row.

area-skill-04.target: I can split a rectangle with side lengths a and b + c into two rectangles and show that its area is a × b + a × c.
area-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can split a rectangle with side lengths a and b + c into two rectangles and show that its area is a × b + a × c.
area-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Adding one side length instead of multiplying both parts by it. Try this: Cut the rectangle on grid paper and write the area of each part before adding.

area-skill-05.target: I can find the area of a rectilinear figure by splitting it into rectangles that do not overlap and adding their areas.
area-skill-05.ifCorrect: You can do this: can find the area of a rectilinear figure by splitting it into rectangles that do not overlap and adding their areas.
area-skill-05.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Counting the overlap twice, or using a side length that belongs to the whole figure for one part. Try this: Shade each rectangle a different color and label its own side lengths before multiplying.
